question: 우리 아바타는 MCCCD처럼 발화, 음성, 얼굴을 같은 구간으로 맞춰서 학습했나요?

turn.text: The avatar did not learn speech, voice, and face in the same interval as MCCCD. The project uses separate inputs for speech-reference preparation, visual assets, and appearance/gesture assets. Voice synthesis is configured separately with a reviewed reference WAV and transcript.

citations.title: Evidence export and multimodal alignment limits
citations.text: The audited workbench exports reviewed text exchanges and source metadata to the dialogue corpus. Speech-reference preparation and visual assets have separate inputs and review records. These serving and export paths do not establish that every text passage has a jointly validated matching audio segment and visible speaking-face segment. Describe MCCCD-style utterance alignment as an intended collection approach unless the exact aligned dataset and its review record are supplied.

citations.title: Configured appearance and gesture assets
citations.text: The studio documentation separates the Gaussian face bundle, a body or rig, and optional learned gesture bundles. Gaussian face data supplies appearance, FLAME data and recorded expression coefficients; gesture data is selected separately. Private asset files and explicit runtime switches are required. The presence of a renderer or a learned-preview switch is not a measured result for facial likeness, natural gesture quality or semantic expression accuracy.

citations.title: Separate reference-conditioned voice synthesis
citations.text: The local launcher configures a separate Qwen voice service with a reviewed reference WAV and its matching transcript. It checks the reference file hashes before starting. External voice endpoints are configurable. Voice reference conditioning is distinct from fine-tuning speech-model weights, and source code does not establish Jensen voice similarity or a measured speed on the presentation machine.
